angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 372,200 km at 67.11 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.9019 +/- 0.0097 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 67.11 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.535 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Piaulet et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-138 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7..206P/abstract): 372,200 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.535 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Piaulet et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-138 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7..206P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3841 +/- 50 K from Piaulet et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-138 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7..206P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Piaulet et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-138 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7..206P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-138.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.710, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-138 (pscomppars): spectral type M1 V, from Kipping et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...28K/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-138 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.18 dex, from Piaulet et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7..206P/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-138 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.25181, from Piaulet et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7..206P/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-138 (pscomppars): age 2.21 Gyr, from Gaidos et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.534.3277G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/ApJS/244/21/table3 (Surface rotation & activity of Kepler stars. I.), column Prot: 19.12 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 19 catalogued periods, 16 of them within 20% of it
